column1: This is the master context for all K CV generation and K Review work. It is the source of truth for candidate facts, tailoring decisions, formatting, and review behavior. Work on individual CVs should be handled in K Review, not copied back into the general chat.
Professional positioning: treasury, financial-risk, derivatives, valuation and investment professional with experience across consulting, banking and the investment side.
Working language for CVs: English unless the user explicitly requests another language. Do not claim German or another language at a level not verified in the source CV or user instructions.
- investment analysis, valuation and transaction finance
The CV must present a coherent analytical finance profile. It must not reduce the candidate to a generic controller, generic consultant or generic private-equity profile.
The strongest long-term direction is analytical work connected to financial markets and real corporate/investment decisions, especially:
- investment analysis where modelling, diligence and financing are central.
The candidate prefers analytical substance, markets and decision support over:
- a role framed only around compliance or routine process work
- an overly junior position when the actual experience supports a more experienced level.
Tailor the emphasis by role rather than forcing one narrative.

Prioritise PwC treasury advisory, the energy-sector secondment, FX/rates/commodity hedging, derivatives valuation, IFRS 9 hedge accounting, liquidity planning, working capital, treasury systems, quantitative risk methods, CFA and FRM.

Prioritise derivatives valuation, market and liquidity risk, VaR, stress testing, Monte Carlo, PCA, GARCH, curve construction, Greeks, R/RStudio, Alteryx, model analysis, financial-risk advisory and CFA/FRM credentials.

Prioritise Rockaway investment analysis, financial-statement analysis, DCF/LBO modelling, cash-flow scenarios, financing structures, terms and covenants, due diligence, valuation and Investment Committee materials. Use PwC transaction and valuation experience where relevant, but do not overemphasise treasury mechanics.
Prioritise the verified energy-sector secondment, commodity-risk hedging, FX management, liquidity planning, renewable-energy PPA advisory and renewable-energy infrastructure analysis.

Prioritise financial modelling, asset/investment analysis, financing structures, diligence, cash-flow scenarios, terms and covenants, valuation and committee materials. Do not claim direct aircraft, engine or helicopter experience unless explicitly added by the user.

Prioritise PwC client work, structured analysis, communication with finance and treasury stakeholders, process and system implementation, leadership of junior colleagues and the ability to translate quantitative analysis into decisions.
- analysis of financing structures, financing terms and covenants

Use this role prominently for investment, corporate-finance, M&A, valuation, infrastructure and financing roles. Do not describe it as pure private-equity sourcing or as a senior portfolio-management role.
### PwC Czech Republic — Junior Manager, Treasury Advisory
- FX, interest-rate and commodity exposure analysis
- derivatives valuation, including forwards, swaps and relevant exotic FX, commodity and equity options
- leadership of a small junior team
- a $50–100 million mandate where the verified CV formulation supports that reference
- RStudio / Power BI risk-tool work where relevant.
### PwC energy-sector secondment — approximately six months
This is verified and must be treated as a distinct project experience when relevant.
- Use selectively for treasury, risk, energy, commodity, infrastructure, corporate-finance and relevant financing roles.
- When the CV has a Selected Project Experience section, show this as its own distinct project item.
- Do not attach it to an unrelated PwC bullet, especially not to the share-based-compensation / fair-value bullet.
- Do not invent the energy company name, exact title, extra dates or responsibilities not provided by the user.
- Keep the wording concise enough to preserve the approved two-page layout.
### Komerční banka — Junior Salesman, Investment Banking
Use when it strengthens a markets, treasury, banking, FX or financial-products narrative. Do not turn this into a pure sales profile.
### Deloitte Czech Republic — Audit Data Analyst Intern
Use selectively for data, accounting, valuation, financial-reporting or analytical consulting roles. Keep it concise in senior applications.
### Charles University — Institute of Economic Studies
Master’s in Economics and Finance, Financial Markets and Banking
- stock ownership structure and related risk premium
Erasmus+ exchange with focus on Alternative Investments.
Do not omit CFA or FRM from a relevant finance, risk, valuation, treasury or quantitative CV. Do not add unverified certificates.
Use only where relevant and keep the list consistent with the Master CV and verified variants:
- Power BI where the relevant project is discussed.
Verified analytical methods and subject areas:
Do not add Python, SQL, programming languages, platforms, products or technical claims unless verified in the current Master CV or explicitly confirmed by the user.
The Master CV uses project experience to surface the most relevant work without changing the underlying employment history.
- PwC energy-sector treasury and accounting secondment
- relevant large valuation or financing mandates where the source CV contains the verified metric.
- use the same bullet font, size, indentation and line spacing as the surrounding bullets
The PwC energy secondment must be a separate Selected Project Experience item when used. It must never be appended awkwardly to another PwC bullet.
Use MASTER(3) as the sole starting document. Other CV variants are reference material only for verified wording, facts, projects, metrics and emphasis.
- no blue redesign and no newly invented modern template
- consistent bold treatment of employer/location header elements
- consistent paragraph spacing and line spacing
- every location label such as Prague, CZ must use the same formatting throughout the document
column2: do not leave one location bold and another normal

column1: - every bullet, including the final PwC fair-value / share-based-compensation bullet, must use the same font size, font face, indentation and line spacing as peer bullets
- Selected Project Experience is a content section, not a reason to redesign the document
- preserve the Master page-break logic so Education, Leadership and Other Information remain in the intended position
- avoid empty pages, orphan headings, clipped text, excessive whitespace and accidental third-page overflow
- do not add a Selected Relevance section unless the user explicitly requests it
- do not alter approved sections merely to make the CV look different.
Every DOCX must be rendered and visually inspected before it is considered complete. Check both pages at full resolution and correct layout defects before registering the package.
- Never invent experience, employers, dates, metrics, responsibilities, languages, transactions, clients or technical tools.
- Do not infer direct aircraft experience from an aviation-finance job description.
- Do not infer German fluency from a German or Austrian role.
- Do not claim that the candidate managed a full treasury function if the verified experience was advisory or analytical.
- Do not overstate Rockaway as a senior investment-committee decision-maker.
- Do not erase the treasury and financial-risk identity when tailoring to M&A.
- Do not erase the investment and transaction-finance experience when tailoring to corporate finance.
- Do not include negative job-search commentary, salary negotiations or reasons for leaving in the CV.
- Do not use generic filler bullets simply to fill a page.
- Keep the candidate’s seniority credible: experienced analyst / junior-manager-level professional with strong cross-functional finance exposure.
- Preserve the distinction between verified facts and role-specific positioning.
Create a role-specific English cover letter unless another language is explicitly requested.
- identify the actual company and role
- explain the most credible connection between the role and the candidate’s experience
- use two or three specific evidence points from the CV
- sound professional and direct, not overly servile
- avoid inventing company facts or responsibilities
- remain concise and normally fit one page
- be saved with the matching package and version.
All individual CV work should happen inside K Review.
- show the job link, CV PDF, CV DOCX and cover letter as separate clickable tiles
- keep the position-specific feedback field empty for a new version
- keep global context separate from position-specific feedback
- maintain one review thread per opportunity
- treat each user message in that thread as authoritative feedback for that role and version
- respond in the same thread with a concise explanation of the change
- create the next version only when feedback is actually submitted
- preserve older versions and never silently overwrite the review history
- register the newest version with valid PDF, DOCX and cover-letter links
- avoid duplicate cards caused by mixing the queue and legacy registry.
The normal review flow is text-based. Screenshots are not required. If legacy attachment support exists, it is optional and must not be presented as a requirement.
The general chat should not be used as the place to conduct individual CV revisions unless the user explicitly asks to move a discussion there."
